paper.title_en: Probing mis-aligned Type-I two-Higgs-doublet model in $\mathrm{e}^+\mathrm{e}^- \to ZH$ at future lepton colliders
paper.abstract_en: A detailed collider study of Higgs production in the process $\mathrm{e}^+\mathrm{e}^- \to ZH$ is presented within the framework of the two-Higgs-doublet model, with particular emphasis on mis-aligned scenarios in the Type-I realization. The analysis is performed at a future $\mathrm{e}^+\mathrm{e}^-$ collider with $\sqrt{s} = 500$ GeV and an integrated luminosity of $10~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, considering heavy Higgs masses in the range $160 \unicode{x2A7D} m_H {\unicode{x2A7D}}400$ GeV. The analysis covers heavy CP-even Higgs states with non-fermionic decay modes such as $H\to WW$ and $H\to hh$, and incorporates final states arising from leptonic and invisible $Z$ boson decays. Fast parameterized detector-level simulations are employed to evaluate selection efficiencies, signal-background discrimination, and exclusion sensitivities. It is shown that values of $|c_{\beta-\alpha}| \gt 0.1$ can be excluded at the $95\%$ confidence level over almost the entire range $1\unicode{x2A7D}\tan\beta{\unicode{x2A7D}}10$ in the $H\to WW$ scenario, while the $H\to hh$ channel provides lower sensitivity.
